Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

We will continue with module seven on functional materials on polymers, and in today's class we are going to study about polymer composites.

Key details

  • We will look at Kevlar synthesis properties and applications and then we will study about reinforced Kevlar composites.
  • In a composite we will have two or more constituent materials and their properties are not attainable by each of these components acting alone.
  • It's only when they are mixed together and form a single material that is known as a composite.
  • When one or more of these components are polymers, we call them as polymer composites.
  • There is always a fiber and a matrix.
  • The matrix would be.
  • Polyester, epoxy, phenolic, silicone, melamine, or a vinyl derivative.
  • And the fiber could be a glass fibre, boron filaments, carbon, graphite fibers, aromate, that is aromatic polyamide, or aluminium fibre.
  • With these two components, the material which is made is known as the polymer composite.
  • They are produced by suitably bonding the fibre material with the polymeric coalescent matrix and curing the same under pressure and heat.
  • Because they have very high strength per unit weight.
  • It is no it is an aromate fibre.
  • What do we mean by aromate fibre?
  • It is aromatic.
  • It is because of the components which are being used, because of the monomers which are being used to make the polymer.
  • Condensation of two monarchs that is one for phenyline diamine and one for benzene di carbone fluoride.
  • thalic acid because these are in the para position the COOH COH groups are in the parapositions so we call it as steal acid and instead of the thalic acid we are using the acid chloride so this becomes steady thaloal chloride.
  • That is because the reactivity will be much more enhanced when we use the teritaloid fluoride.
  • It is 14 phenyline dye.
  • Again, these two are in the para position.
  • The amine groups are in the para position.
  • polymerization which will take place, the condensate condensation reaction would.
  • Result in elimination of an HCl molecule.
  • So like this, these two monomers are because they have.
  • Two functional groups each.
  • So if this condensation happens, this side is still open for the next diamine to attach, and similarly this NH2 is open for the next.
  • COCL group to attach.
  • So therefore the polymerization continues this way, and what we get is amide linkages between these monomers and we get Keblar.
  • How did we get it?
  • It is a condensation polymer.
  • Kevlar is known to be five times stronger than steel on an equal weight basis.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Firstly, let us understand what is a composite.
  • Let us study about Kevlar, which is a very important fibre.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

All of us know that Kebler is used to make bulletproof jackets.

Key details

  • The first reason is that there is extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding which is taking place between the Kevlar chains.
  • chain and so on so many chains are there in Kebler now between these chains there is formation of hydrogen bond now we know that between the polymer units itself the when we join the units monomer units the leakage which we are getting is an amide linkage.
  • Then again here we have CO NH.
  • NH C O.
  • So this is getting repeated, and here again in the same way in the next chain also we see there is C O N H N H C O C O N H N H C O.
  • This is one thing we need to pay attention to that once we have.
  • NH group here and CO here, the next one cannot be NH and CO, it has to be CO and NH because it is formed from the diamine, so NH and NH and then again we have CO that is the amide linkage here.
  • And then so we see that there are amide linkages and but between the cablar chains now we have strong hydrogen bonding which is taking place.
  • How is it happening between the carbonyl groups and the NH centers.
  • that the hydrogen and the oxygen the hydrogen of the amine and the oxygen of the CO are coming very close, they are very in close proximity and that would result in formation of hydrogen bond.
  • So there are so many hydrogen bonds possible because repeatedly every unit there is a CONH group and these N of one the hydrogen of one of the chains and the.
  • O of the other chain they are coming in close proximity, and that will result in formation of hydrogen bond.
  • Now because of this aromatic ring, this is giving a lot of firmness to Kepler.
  • If it's an elephatic chain, we know it will be more flexible.
  • Whereas now it is in the form of an aromatic ring.
  • And that is giving firmness to Kevlar.
  • And another reason for this is aromatic stacking.
  • To the polymer, and therefore we find that keevlar is very strong.
  • The answer is there are two reasons.
  • One is the extensive hydrogen bonding.
  • between chains of kevlar and additional strength is coming from aromatic stacking.
  • What are the properties of Kevlar?
  • We saw the structure and based on that we know that properties are going to depend on the structure.
  • It has high strength to weight ratio and very high chemical inertness, low coefficient of thermal expansion.
  • It also has flame resistance and high impact and cut resistance and textile processability.

Core explanation · 10:00–14:59

Based on all these properties now we can understand that there will be a lot of applications of Kevlar.

Key details

  • Then gloves, sleeves, jackets, etcetera are made of Kevlar to protect users from cuts and heat.
  • And then inner lining in bicycle tires, then lightweight boot hulls, aircraft panels, race cars, bridge structure.
  • Earlier they used to use steel pipes.
  • Now we know that when this is in happening offshore there will be in the ocean and therefore there'll be a lot of salinity and corrosion is very rampant over there.
  • ropes in offshore drilling.
  • What are they?
  • Special cutting scissors and drilling machines are required because it's a very strong material.
  • And one more problem here is that the fibre is hygroscopic.
  • We have still not formed the composite because when we talk of a composite, we know there are two components.
  • Obviously, we need a matrix for that and that matrix is usually an epoxy resin.
  • And now the material will become so strong that it is going to now have many more applications.
  • This matrix when you have and these fibers are embedded in it, then any force which is applied onto the material will be dissipated the impact is going to be taken by the metric so that makes the material even more strong.
  • This is known as reinforced Kevlar composites.
  • tennis and tennis and squash rackets.
  • So now the applications have increased because the material is still more stronger as compared to Kepler.
  • Kevlar on the next class we will talk of another polymer composite and that is carbon fiber.
